successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: Warmia, the bishop's secular third of the diocese (Braniewo, Frombork, Orneta, Lidzbark Warmiński, Reszel, Barczewo, Olsztyn), about 4,500 km2 on the Warmia page

ledger.x: 1243: William of Modena founds the Bishopric of Ermland in Prussia.

20 September 1260: 'The major revolt began on 20 September 1260' (Great Prussian Uprising); the Warmians under Glappe rose, and 'the rebel headquarters' were at Heilsberg (Lidzbark), in the bishop's domain.

1274: 'the uprising was ended in 1274' with the capture of Heilsberg; 'Natangians and Warmians had also accepted baptism and promised their loyalty to the Knights' by 1277 (old-prussians books the end in 1277).
1280: the seat moves from Braunsberg to Frauenburg (Frombork) 'after attacks by heathen Old Prussians'.
1306: Lidzbark Warmiński 'became the seat for the Bishopric of Warmia, and remained the Prince-Bishop's seat for 500 years'; Frauenburg remains the cathedral see.
July 1626: after landing at Pillau on 6 July 1626 the Swedes 'rapidly occupied Braniewo, Frombork, Elbląg, Orneta, and Malbork'.
July 1626: Orneta occupied in the same sweep.
September 1629: the truce left Sweden 'the towns of Braunsberg, Frauenberg, and Elbing' in Royal Prussia; Orneta is not on that list, so it returns.
12 September 1635: the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf 'returned these gains' and Sweden withdrew from Prussia.
1772: 'the Kingdom of Prussia annexed and secularised the prince-bishopric as a state'; it 'was incorporated into the newly formed Prussian province of East Prussia in 1773'.
1772: the last prince-bishop, Ignacy Krasicki (1766-1772), loses the principality to Prussia.

wars.name: Great Prussian Uprising
wars.outcome: The revolt began on 20 September 1260; the Knights captured the rebel headquarters at Heilsberg in 1274, 'the uprising was ended in 1274', and the Warmians accepted baptism and loyalty by 1277.

wars.name: Thirteen Years' War
wars.outcome: The Warmian nobility and towns joined the Prussian Confederation (1440); the king signed the act of incorporation on 6 March 1454; the bishopric sided with Poland in 1464; the Peace of Thorn of 1466 had the Order renounce claims.

wars.name: War of the Priests
wars.outcome: A conflict 'over the right to name and approve Bishops in Warmia'; the Polish king accepted Tüngen as prince-bishop at the First Treaty of Piotrków.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1626-1629)
wars.outcome: Gustavus Adolphus landed at Pillau on 6 July 1626 and took Braniewo, Frombork and Orneta; Sweden retained Braunsberg and Frauenberg under the 1629 truce until the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf (12 September 1635).

certainty.note: The frontier with the Old Prussians and the Order's land was being settled by conquest and partition; the 1260-1274 uprising contested it.
The Golden Bull of 1356 confirmed the bishop's one third of the diocese as a secular domain; the page gives no survey, and the drawn polygon is a stand-in cut to the Warmia page's 4,500 km2.
